Definition: galbanam, an odorous gum (as if fatty)
BiblicalUsage: Galbanum is one of the sweet spices of the holy incense, taken with stacte and onycha and pure frankincense, each of like weight. It is a resin that burns sweet before the LORD.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe God names the ingredients of His incense because worship is exact: every spice in its measure, and the smell rises as He commanded.
